html:
A huge eruption of the Ilopango volcano, now a lake near San Salvador in El Salvador, one of the largest in Central America in the last several thousand years. Recent dating puts it around 431 CE; earlier estimates ranged from the 200s to about 540.

It spread a thick layer of white ash over much of what is now El Salvador. Farmland near the volcano was buried, and many Maya towns in the area were abandoned for generations. People likely fled to Guatemala and Honduras, perhaps adding to the growth of other Maya centres. The village of Joya de Cerén, buried by a smaller local eruption later on, gives an idea of life in the region at the time.

The eruption sent sulfur into the upper air and probably cooled the climate for a few years. Some once linked it to the volcanic winter of 536, but the new date makes that unlikely.
